plans.title: Fix the .m4a decode contract: an explicit ffmpeg/soxr backend, and the pins that keep it working
notes: Opened from residual iter-2026-09-qwen3-asr-closeout R5 (high), found by the deep PR review of #19 (verdict blocked). The .m4a codec fallback is inert under the librosa that the repo's own declarations resolve, because librosa 1.0.0 dropped audioread and load() is now a bare soundfile call.

Decision recorded before implementation: replace librosa with an explicit backend — ffmpeg for decode (already an AGENTS.md requirement, already shelled to at audio.py:71-81) and soxr for resampling (bit-identical to librosa.resample's default soxr_hq, 200 KB wheel, numpy-only).

Blast radius found while deciding, larger than R5's title: librosa 1.0.0 requires numpy>=2.1.0, while the verified ROCm host runs numpy 1.26.4 — the unbounded extra would drag numpy 2.x into a verified GPU environment, not merely break AAC decode.

Done 2026-09-27 (f4c0ebb). Chose the explicit-backend option over bounding librosa: ffmpeg is already an AGENTS.md requirement and already shelled to by audio.py, soxr is what librosa.resample calls at its default res_type, and both were measured (ffmpeg path bit-identical to f32le; soxr bit-identical to librosa.resample). Also closed 20260924-qwen3-asr-transformers R1 and R2, whose owed follow-ups (a real .m4a fixture; a DEFAULT_HOTWORDS pin) this commit supplies. Residual R5 itself closed. Not yet merged to main: the branch is pushed/mergeable work, the PR is the next step.

Phase 4/5 2026-09-27: branch pushed (b43234b) and PR #20 opened against main. The repository configures no CI and has no review threads, so the merge-ready gates are satisfied vacuously. The merge itself is the operator's; until it lands this lifecycle is not delivered.

Phase 5 review round 2026-09-27: three adversarial seats (runtime / tests / docs+deps) reviewed the whole branch against a pinned diff pack. Findings answered in 902879c (revert the lock regeneration — two seats independently found it installed a PyPI CUDA torch on the ROCm host), e766f23 (four test coverage holes, mutation-verified) and d6153b8 (four refuted claims). One of my own mistakes was corrected mid-review (a citation pointing at asr.py:316 instead of :351), which moved the tree under the seats; recorded rather than smoothed over. Residuals: R5 resolved, R1/R2 resolved, R6 REOPENED (its earlier closure credited the reverted lock fix), R7 registered high. ASR suite 49 passed; full suite 1713 passed / 6 skipped / 0 failed. PR body corrected to match.

Phase 6 2026-09-27: merged as d356e16 (merge commit; d6153b8 is an ancestor, so not squashed). Post-merge verified against an archive of the merged main, not the scratch tree: 1713 passed / 6 skipped / 0 failed, decode works with no librosa, hotword list 33 entries with the withdrawn acronyms absent, and uv.lock unchanged. Lifecycle closed.

Compound 2026-09-27: performed, not skipped — landed as 94430fd on main. Two docs updated (wsl-rocm-gpu-asr §2b; absence-assertion-negative-control instances), zero created, both Q5 high-overlap. The package README's promotion log was empty and is now filled (6 rows); premise-freshness-before-lock.md gained its missing Promoted-from trace. store.db absent, so no catalog row written and none claimed.
